Article Title: India probes Pernod Ricard, Diageo over Scotch whisky imports under UK trade pact
Article Text:
File photo: Bottles of Absolut vodka, produced by Pernod Ricard, are displayed at a wine shop (Picture credit: Reuters)

Companies say they are cooperating with authorities

India-UK trade pact cuts Scotch import tariffs

Pernod faces other regulatory challenges

Indian tax authorities are investigating whether liquor makers Pernod Ricard and Diageo wrongly classified bulk Scotch whisky imports to claim lower tariffs under the India-UK trade agreement, Reuters reported, citing five industry sources familiar with the matter.The investigation centres on whether the companies were eligible for the reduced import duty introduced under the pact, which came into effect on July 15.India agreed to cut tariffs on certain Scotch imports to 75 per cent from 150 per cent.However, tax inspectors have argued that the duty reduction does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, four people familiar with the matter told Reuters.“The tax department is concerned that bulk imports are being wrongly classified,” one of the sources said.Last week, tax inspectors visited Pernod Ricard's India headquarters near New Delhi and questioned company executives about its Scotch imports, three sources told Reuters.During the visit on Thursday, officials reviewed documents related to bulk imports, although they have not contacted the company again since, one source said.Diageo's Indian unit, United Spirits, disclosed in a stock exchange filing last week that its offices at multiple locations had been searched on Friday as part of an “industry-wide exercise” by authorities.The company did not specify the subject of the searches.Two sources told Reuters that Diageo was also under investigation over the classification of some Scotch imports.Pernod Ricard told Reuters that it was cooperating with the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and providing all the information requested by officials. The company said it was committed to addressing any questions raised by the authorities.Diageo also said it was cooperating with Indian authorities and had always complied with local laws. In its stock exchange disclosure, United Spirits said it had provided all documents and clarifications sought.The investigation comes amid longstanding disputes between foreign companies and Indian tax authorities over import classifications and tariff payments.Such disputes have involved companies including Samsung, LG and Volkswagen, with officials often raising substantial back-tax demands years after goods were imported.Pernod Ricard, a French company, and Britain's Diageo dominate India's $65 billion alcohol market, according to Reuters. Both import bulk Scotch concentrates, which are mixed with other ingredients to produce brands such as Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell's.The India-UK trade agreement reduced import tariffs on certain Scotch products by half, from 150 per cent to 75 per cent, from July 15. The tariff is scheduled to fall further to 40 per cent over the next 10 years.The lower duties have already led to price cuts for some imported Scotch whiskies in several states. Diageo and Pernod Ricard reduced prices by around 10-15 per cent for selected products in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Goa and Uttar Pradesh.Brands affected included Diageo's Johnnie Walker Black Label and J&B, while Pernod Ricard sought approval for lower prices for Chivas, Ballantine's and The Glenlivet.The British government said in July that “iconic UK products”, including whisky and gin, would benefit from India's tariff reductions. UK whisky exports to India were worth more than £200 million in 2022, according to the British government.Crisil Ratings said this year that the UK accounts for nearly 75 per cent of India's imported spirits market, primarily driven by Scotch whisky.Pernod Ricard is also facing antitrust cases in India, its largest market by volume, as well as a $314 million back-tax demand over allegations that it undervalued certain imports. The company denies wrongdoing.Diageo, meanwhile, agreed in August to reformulate some of its popular drinks after India's food safety regulator banned them in some states over the addition of flavours that allegedly breached regulations.The latest investigation focuses on whether the companies' declarations for bulk Scotch imports qualified for the lower duties under the India-UK trade agreement.
Article Summary: India-UK trade pact cuts Scotch import tariffs to 75 per cent from 150 per cent. But tax inspectors have argued that the duty reduction does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, four people familiar with the matter said. Pernod Ricard and Britain's Diageo dominate India's $65 billion alcohol market.

Article Title: Crude holds near $110 per barrel as Middle East tensions keep supply concerns alive
Article Text:
Brent crude hovers near $110 per barrel

Houthi attacks add to supply concerns

Oil prices hovered near $110 a barrel on Tuesday as traders assessed the impact of Washington’s decision to ease some restrictions on Russian energy exports, while fresh attacks claimed by Yemen’s Houthis against Saudi targets added to concerns over potential supply disruptions in the Middle East.WTI crude was trading at $98.72, up 18 cents, or 0.18%, while Brent crude stood at $109.70, gaining 16 cents, or 0.15%. Brent had climbed to $110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest level since May 20.The market was weighing the possibility of additional Russian oil and fuel supplies following an executive order issued by US President Donald Trump on Friday night. The order waived key Russia-related US sanctions and tariffs, including duties on Russian goods and penalties for purchasing the country’s oil and gas. However, Trump said on Saturday that he had yet to announce a final decision, while Secretary of State Marco Rubio said officials needed more time to assess the situation.Russia’s crude oil production rose by 65,000 barrels per day in September to 8.43 million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency last week. Despite the increase, output remained around 870,000 barrels per day below the level recorded a year earlier.The prospect of more Russian supplies has offered a possible counterweight to concerns about disruptions elsewhere, but risks to energy infrastructure in the Gulf region remain a key concern for traders.Fresh security concerns emerged after Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they had carried out several attacks targeting Saudi energy, airport and military facilities. The sites named included an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and Abha airport.Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claims, and Reuters could not independently verify them.Separately, an attack by the Houthis on a government security forces training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province on Monday killed 58 people and injured more than 200.The latest attacks have added to concerns about regional stability and the safety of energy supplies, helping keep oil prices above the $100-a-barrel mark despite the prospect of increased Russian supply.
Article Summary: WTI crude was trading at $98.72, up 18 cents, or 0.18%, while Brent crude stood at $109.70. Brent had climbed to $110.70 a barrel in the previous session, its highest level since May 20. Fresh attacks claimed by Yemen’s Houthis against Saudi targets added to concerns over potential supply disruptions.

Article Title: Rupee rises to 94.80 against US dollar, but crude oil threatens recovery
Article Text:
Rupee strengthens against US dollar

NEW DELHI: Rupee began the week on a cheerful note, inching towards the 94 mark against US dollar on Monday. The currency strengthened by 9 paise to 94.80 against the greenback in early trade, extending its recovery for a third consecutive session. This followed Friday's close of 94.89, when the currency had gained 10 paise.The Reserve Bank of India 's structural forex interventions continued to support rupee, although elevated crude oil prices remain a key risk to sustaining the gains.Forex traders said that the currency has staged its sharpest rally in seven months, but sustained pressure from expensive crude, rising US treasury yields and continued foreign capital outflows has kept the currency under strain. The RBI has stepped up its market interventions amid these pressures.CR forex advisors MD Amit Pabari said the currency's movement below 95 over the past three sessions has brought the 94.80–94.70 range into focus."With USDINR holding below 95.00 for the last 3 sessions, the focus shifts to 94.80–94.70. A sustained break below 94.80 could open the way towards 94.00 over the coming weeks."However, elevated crude prices remain a key risk, and the rupee's next move will depend on whether oil eases or sustains its surge," he added.Brent crude, which had surged to $110 per barrel, was trading at $107.79 per barrel in futures trade, down 1.88%. Attacks on commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz, interruptions to oil flows and threats to Saudi energy infrastructure have fuelled concerns about a prolonged supply shock.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six currencies, stood at 101.83, marginally lower by 0.01%.Meanwhile, domestic equities came under pressure in early trade. The BSE Sensex shed 470.50 points to reach 74,318, while NSE Nifty50 declined 147.10 points to 22,999.05.Foreign investors, however, returned as net buyers of Indian equities on Friday. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) purchased shares worth Rs 1,165.92 crore on a net basis, according to exchange data.The country's forex reserves also registered another weekly decline. Reserve Bank of India data released on Friday showed that reserves fell by USD 8.578 billion to USD 726.027 billion in the week ended October 9.The fall followed a $12.952 billion decline in the preceding reporting week, which had brought India's foreign exchange reserves down to $734.606 billion.
Article Summary: Rupee inching towards 94 mark against US dollar on Monday. Currency strengthened by 9 paise to 94.80 against the greenback in early trade. This followed Friday's close of 94.89, when the currency had gained 10 paise.

Article Title: Nepal bans Priyagold biscuit after FSSAI finds serious hygiene deficiencies
Article Text:
Representational image

Nepal has barred the import, sale and distribution of Priyagold biscuits made by India based Surya Food and Agro Ltd, after food safety concerns flagged by Indian authorities.Nepal’s Food Technology and Quality Control Department (FTQCD) announced the restrictions in a notice issued on Monday, classifying the biscuits as sub-standard. The move follows action by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has suspended the manufacturer's licence and initiated legal proceedings for prosecution.According to FSSAI, an inspection of Surya Food and Agro revealed serious deficiencies in food safety and hygiene. The regulator also initiated prosecution proceedings against the company for using cattle feed bran in the manufacture of Priyagold biscuits, along with other serious violations.Citing FSSAI’s notice, Nepal's food department decided to prohibit the biscuits from entering or being sold in the country. The decision was taken during an emergency meeting held virtually at the initiative of department director general Sanjeev Kumar Karna.The department said that the restrictions were imposed with human health security and consumer welfare in mind.Following the ban, the FTQCD has asked relevant bodies, traders and consumers to refrain from importing Priyagold biscuits and ensure that their sale and distribution are stopped.It has also directed authorised importers and food traders to immediately recall any stocks of the biscuits that may still be available in the market.
Article Summary: Nepal has barred the import, sale and distribution of Priyagold biscuits made by India based Surya Food and Agro Ltd. The move follows action by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has suspended the manufacturer's licence and initiated legal proceedings for prosecution.

Article Title: No buyers, higher costs: US homebuilder confidence hits 14-year low
Article Text:
US homebuilder confidence hits 14-year low as costs soar

Price cuts and incentives rise as buyers hold back

Housing affordability remains a concern ahead of US midterms

US homebuilder confidence fell to its lowest level in more than 14 years in October, with rising mortgage rates, expensive construction materials and labour shortages weighing on the housing market, according to a survey released on Monday.The National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index slipped three points to 29, its weakest reading since June 2012. The decline was steeper than economists polled by Reuters had anticipated, with their forecast standing at 31.The Middle East conflict has pushed up energy prices and borrowing costs, adding to the financial pressure on builders. Mortgage rates have climbed alongside Treasury yields as the US-Israeli war with Iran fuels inflation. Freddie Mac data showed that the average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage reached 7.40% last week, its highest level in nearly three years.Higher borrowing costs are weighing on home sales, while tariffs on imports have added to construction expenses. Builders are also facing labour shortages amid an immigration crackdown."Builders are also contending with higher costs for construction loans, building materials and diesel, as well as persistent labor shortages," said NAHB chairman Bill Owens."Nationwide, more than one-third of builders reported immigration enforcement activity in their market areas during the past month, causing construction delays and discouraging legal workers from reporting to work."Weak demand has left builders with a growing stock of unsold new homes, making them more reluctant to start construction on additional single-family housing projects.To attract buyers, 43% of builders reported reducing prices in October, the highest proportion recorded during the 2020-2026 period. The average price cut remained at 6% for the seventh consecutive month. Meanwhile, 65% of builders offered sales incentives, marking the 19th month in a row that at least 60% have resorted to such measures.The survey also showed deterioration across all three measures of housing market activity. The index measuring current sales conditions fell two points to 33, while expectations for sales over the coming months dropped five points to 32. Prospective buyer traffic also declined five points to 18."Higher mortgage rates, elevated construction costs and weaker consumer confidence are keeping more buyers on the sidelines," said Robert Dietz, NAHB chief economist. "As a result, buyer traffic has fallen to its lowest level since April 2012, excluding the pandemic's onset in April 2020."The combination of high mortgage rates and persistently expensive homes has placed housing affordability at the centre of economic concerns ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress.President Donald Trump earlier this year declined to sign a bipartisan bill aimed at improving housing affordability, dismissing it as "a big yawn". He instead pressed Congress, including fellow Republicans who resisted his demands, to first pass separate and contentious voting requirements.The latest survey highlights the continuing challenges facing homebuilders as higher costs and subdued buyer demand affect their decisions on pricing, incentives and new construction.
Article Summary: US homebuilder confidence fell to its lowest level in more than 14 years in October. Rising mortgage rates, expensive construction materials and labour shortages are weighing on the housing market. Mortgage rates have climbed alongside Treasury yields as the US-Israeli war with Iran fuels inflation.

Article Title: Urea import prices hit 15-month low, but fertiliser subsidy burden may rise marginally due to higher DAP & Sulphur rates
Article Text:
Urea import prices have seen a significant decline, now standing at $392 per tonne, a notable drop from previous months.

New Delhi: The import price of urea fell to $392 per tonne in Sept, its lowest level since June 2025 and nearly 59% below the peak of $947 per tonne recorded in May this year. This is expected to ease pressure on govt’s fertiliser subsidy bill, which was expected to rise sharply amid the West Asia crisis.However, elevated prices of diammonium phosphate (DAP), muriate of potash (MOP) and sulphur are likely to push the subsidy outgo in 2026-27 by Rs 20,000-25,000 crore above the Rs 2.17 lakh crore budget allocation. This is still much less than the govt’s internal estimates during the major supply disruptions in April-May, which had pegged the fertiliser subsidy bill at around Rs 3 lakh crore.Govt data show that the import price of diammonium phosphate (DAP) declined by barely 3% to $906 per tonne in Sept from its peak of $933 in June, while sulphur prices have surged to a record level above $1,000 per tonne, registering over 200% increase compared to last year. However, this will not impact farmers, who will continue to get these fertilisers at subsided rates.Urea import prices have fallen sharply due to easing international prices and improved supply with India diversifying sources. One of the main reasons is China renewing urea exports, which has increased competition among sellers. TOI has learnt that there is an overwhelming response to recently issued global tenders.“We don’t expect urea prices to go up in near future and India has good stock of the fertiliser for the upcoming Rabi season,” said an industry insider.To reduce dependency on only a few countries, India has diversified import of sugar from nations, including Oman, Malaysia, Vietnam, Georgia, Nigeria, Russia, Finland, Egypt, Algeria, Turkey, and the Netherlands.In the case of DAP, the import prices have fallen marginally from the peak of $933 per tonne in May to $906 in Sept, which is still higher than a year ago, because of sulphur shortage, rising phosphoric acid costs and supply disruptions keeping phosphatic fertiliser production expensive.As far as surge in sulphur import price is concerned, this has been primarily because the West Asia conflict has disrupted supplies from the world’s largest exporting region and attacks on Russian energy infrastructure have further tightened availability.
Article Summary: Urea import prices have seen a significant decline, now standing at $392 per tonne. This is expected to ease pressure on govt’s fertiliser subsidy bill, which was expected to rise sharply amid the West Asia crisis. However, elevated prices of diammonium phosphate (DAP), muriate of potash (MOP) and sulphur are likely to push the subsidy outgo in 2026-27 by Rs 20,000-25,000 crore.

Article Title: Husband and wife sell property; Income Tax dept alleges Rs 3.30 crore sale against Rs 1.60 crore in deed, cites WhatsApp chats, Excel sheets to claim Rs 1.70 crore cash receipts, but ITAT gives relief
Article Text:
The AO treated the alleged amount as undisclosed cash receipts and made an addition under Section 69A. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the taxpayer win relief?

Significance of ruling

Property related transactions can sometimes be complicated. Recording the same in your income tax return is equally important. But what if the Income Tax Department sends you a notice for unexplained cash receipts, believing that you have received a part of the payment for property sale in cash.In one such case, the tax department relied on WhatsApp messages and Excel spreadsheets to reach the conclusion that the property had been sold for an amount higher than the one disclosed. The assessee finally won the case in Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Delhi.The dispute concerned a man and his wife, who jointly owned a property in Delhi before selling it.The Income Tax Department alleged that the buyers had paid an additional amount in cash beyond the sale consideration documented in the registered conveyance deed.Also Read | Man sold his house and bought a Rs 1.10 crore flat jointly with wife; income tax department denies Rs 55.48 lakh capital gains exemption for half the amount, but ITAT Mumbai gives full relief The assessing officer calculated the total transaction value at around Rs 3.30 crore, whereas the registered sale deed recorded a consideration of Rs 1.60 crore. The department regarded the difference of Rs 1.70 crore as cash received by the sellers but not disclosed in the documents.The case arose from a search conducted in 2021, involving a group of companies. According to the tax department, an Excel workbook titled “BOSS -DEC 18 onwards”, handwritten diary entries and other seized material pointed to cash payments allegedly made to the man in connection with a property in Delhi, jointly owned by him and his wife.The department alleged that Rs 1.70 crore had been paid in cash by the group owner in connection with the property transaction to the husband and wife. Its case included entries for Rs 1.55 crore and a further Rs 15 lakh. It also relied on handwritten records and WhatsApp conversations involving several people.The Assessing Officer (AO) also drew on WhatsApp conversations that mentioned payments of Rs 50 lakh, Rs 50 lakh, Rs 20 lakh, Rs 5 lakh and Rs 30 lakh. These amounts added up to Rs 1.55 crore.The AO treated the alleged amount as undisclosed cash receipts and made an addition under Section 69A read with Section 115BBE of the Income Tax Act. The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) subsequently sustained an addition of Rs 1,16,25,000 out of the Rs 1.70 crore assessed, giving part relief.However the man appealed in ITAT.Also Read | He inherited land from mother, redeveloped home & received Rs 75 lakh from builder; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT Delhi gives relief, ruling multiple floors can qualify as one house The man’s representative disputed the reliance on the seized material and argued that he had not been given a proper opportunity to cross-examine the people whose statements and communications were used against him.He also challenged the legality of the proceedings under Section 153C, including the recording of a consolidated satisfaction note covering seven assessment years.The taxpayer further argued that the alleged cash consideration related to a property sold through a registered conveyance deed dated October 31, 2019, falling in assessment year 2020-21, rather than the assessment year under appeal, 2019-20.The tribunal found that the WhatsApp conversations relied upon by the tax authorities largely contained monetary figures but did not clearly establish what the payments were for or the purpose behind them.“The WhatsApp chats and seized documents merely referred to certain figures and alleged transactions but did not conclusively establish that the assessee had received unaccounted cash,” CA Avinash Kumar Rao, Partner at Mohindra & Associates told ET.CA Suresh Surana said the assessing officer had also not adequately examined the people connected with the alleged payments. The taxpayer was not given a proper opportunity to cross-examine them.Also Read | Man had Rs 2 crore bank deposit and didn’t file ITR, faced Rs 2.51 crore tax addition; ITAT Chennai quashes reassessment after Income Tax Department missed 6-year deadline by 5 days The tribunal also noted that the Income Tax Department had not summoned a man despite relying substantially on his statement and documents recovered from him to support its allegations.The tribunal observed that if the department intended to rely on the chats and related material as evidence of cash consideration, “it was essential for the assessing officer to have examined these persons on oath and also give the assessee an opportunity to cross-examine these persons.”It explained that WhatsApp messages and supporting documents needed to be properly tested rather than treated as conclusive proof. As the order put it, “the inferences drawn cannot be considered to be conclusively based on relevant and admissible evidence, but become more of suspicious circumstance” if the necessary examination and opportunity to challenge the evidence are missing.The Income Tax Department had also relied on a common satisfaction note covering seven assessment years. However, it had not identified relevant incriminating material for every assessment year included in the note.Surana explains that the ITAT held that the department was required to demonstrate a clear link between the material seized during the search and the income relating to each individual assessment year before initiating proceedings under Section 153C.On these grounds, the tribunal allowed both the quantum appeal and the consequential penalty appeal. Its final direction was explicit: “The impugned assessment and penalty stands quashed.”The order was pronounced on September 9, 2026.It’s important to note that the decision turned on the evidentiary shortcomings and legal defects identified by the tribunal; it should not be read as a finding that the alleged cash payments definitely did not occur.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claim The decision reiterates a fundamental principle of tax law: even strong suspicion cannot take the place of conclusive evidence. The Income Tax Department can examine WhatsApp conversations, Excel spreadsheets and handwritten records, but simply finding such material does not automatically prove that a taxpayer earned undisclosed income.CA Avinash Kumar Rao advises taxpayers facing allegations based on third-party statements or conversations to obtain copies of the material cited against them and assess its context and relevance. They should also ask for an opportunity to cross-examine the individuals concerned. Such requests are preferably made in writing while the assessment proceedings are underway.The ruling also underlines that procedural safeguards prescribed under the Income-tax Act must be followed rather than treated as formal requirements that can be overlooked.
Article Summary: The Income Tax Department alleged that the buyers had paid an additional amount in cash beyond the sale consideration documented in the registered conveyance deed. The department regarded the difference of Rs 1.70 crore as cash received by the sellers but not disclosed in the documents. The case arose from a search conducted in 2021, involving a group of companies.

Article Title: In-kind welfare: 22 crore move up consumption ladder
Article Text:
The findings also highlighted a distinct regional divergence in welfare impact

Which state saw most gains

NEW DELHI: In-kind social transfers ranging from free foodgrains under the public distribution system (PDS) to laptops, bicycles and school uniforms have pushed nearly 22 crore people -- comprising around 19% of rural population and 8.4% of those in urban areas -- into higher consumption brackets, a new study in an NSO journal showed.Using the household consumption expenditure survey (HCES) 2022–23 unit-level data, the NSO study concluded that 15.8% of the population at the national level saw improvement in their level of living as they moved into higher monthly per capita consumption expenditure (MPCE) category once the monetary value of free goods was imputed.Incorporating these welfare measures also reduced consumption inequality, measured by Gini coefficient, pointing to a boost in effective purchasing power as it freed up some cash that would have been allocated for buying some of these goods.The findings also highlighted a distinct regional divergence in welfare impact. West Bengal led with over 40% of its total population (46.5% rural and 24.9% urban) transitioning to higher consumption brackets due to in-kind transfers. This was followed by Chhattisgarh (29.2%), Assam (29%), Karnataka (28.4%), and Uttar Pradesh (22.7%). In contrast, industrialised and higher-baseline states reported significantly lower transition rates, with Gujarat seeing only 3.7% population transitioning to a higher consumption bracket, followed by Kerala (4.6%) and Haryana (7.1%).Despite concerns over several of such transfers being populist in nature, often announced ahead of elections, the study concluded that in-kind social welfare acted as a progressive measure as maximum upward mobility was concentrated at the bottom of the pyramid, indicating that welfare benefits effectively reach the targeted, lower-income households.Researchers, however, noted that the 22-crore figure was a conservative estimate as major public services, specifically free healthcare benefits under schemes such as Ayushman Bharat (PM-JAY) and free school education were excluded from the calculations due to survey design limitations. Factoring in the out-of-pocket savings from health and education would indicate an even broader elevation of living standards across Indian households, it said.
Article Summary: West Bengal led with over 40% of its total population transitioning to higher consumption brackets due to in-kind transfers. In contrast, industrialised and higher-baseline states reported significantly lower transition rates. Gujarat saw only 3.7% population transitioned to a higher consumption bracket, followed by Kerala and Haryana.

Article Title: ‘SC order won’t impact growth’: Yes Bank
Article Text:
In an earnings call, managing director and CEO Vinay Tonse said the bank was examining the judgment and its options

MUMBAI: Yes Bank has told investors that Supreme Court’s order to restore Rs 8,415 crore of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds written off during its March 2020 restructuring would not constrain growth, citing deferred tax assets (DTAs) and other capital buffers to absorb the impact. Rating agencies said the ruling would not materially affect the bank’s credit profile, although it has implications for its capital structure.Crisil Ratings said Yes Bank could absorb the AT1 bond ruling’s impact through internal accruals and fresh capital, with support expected from its largest shareholder, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation. While the ruling is not expected to materially affect its credit profile, coupon payments for the intervening 5.5 years remain uncertain. In another case, Dhanlaxmi Bank was earlier allowed to defer coupons on Basel II-compliant tier-II bonds.Analysts said reversing the AT1 write-down, originally credited to the profit and loss account, could leave the bank without the profits needed to pay coupons under the conditions of the AT1 bonds. As a result, the bank’s maximum liability was likely to be Rs 8,415 crore.In an earnings call, managing director and CEO Vinay Tonse said the bank was examining the judgment and its options.“We respect the judgment and are examining it carefully, including the options available to the bank,” he said.CFO Niranjan Banodkar said reinstating the AT1 principal would reduce the common equity tier-I (CET-1) ratio by around 240 basis points on a pro forma basis, based on an indicative assessment as of Sept 30, 2026, including profits. The overall tier-I capital ratio would remain around 13.7%, while the pro forma CET-1 ratio would be 11.4%. Banodkar said the bank was reviewing the judgment, legal options and capital plans.
Article Summary: Yes Bank has told investors that Supreme Court’s order to restore Rs 8,415 crore of additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds written off during its March 2020 restructuring would not constrain growth. Rating agencies said the ruling would not materially affect the bank's credit profile. In an earnings call, managing director and CEO Vinay Tonse said the bank was examining the judgment.

Article Title: Harish Bhat resigns from Trent board after 12 years
Article Text:
In his resignation letter to Noel, Bhat described his tenure on Trent’s board as a “pleasure and privilege”

MUMBAI: Harish Bhat, a long-serving Tata executive, has resigned from Trent, the retailer chaired by Noel Tata, citing growing personal and professional commitments.Bhat, 63, served on Trent’s board for 12 years. An alumnus of BITS Pilani and IIM Ahmedabad, he continues to serve on the boards of Tata Starbucks and Infiniti Retail (Croma).In his resignation letter to Noel, Bhat described his tenure on Trent’s board as a “pleasure and privilege”, crediting Tata’s leadership for the company’s rapid growth and transformation.Bhat is the only member of former Tata Sons chairman Cyrus Mistry ’s inner circle to remain within the Tata group after Mistry’s acrimonious split with the conglomerate in 2016.His resignation has revived debate about shifting loyalties within India’s largest conglomerate. Nirmalya Kumar, who also served on Mistry’s core team, wrote in a LinkedIn post that Bhat was “the first, and only member” of the group executive council “to switch sides to the new regime when Mistry was fired and go to the press with it”. Kumar argued that the move helped secure Bhat’s position during current chairman N Chandrasekaran’s era, albeit at a cost. “The reward was continued employment during N Chandrasekaran era with a honorific title but no power”.As the balance of power gradually shifts towards Noel, some Tata group observers see Bhat’s departure as another sign of changing dynamics within the conglomerate. Kumar, who returned to academia after his stint with the Tata group, said the transition was prompting a fresh realignment of loyalties. “Now tables are turning from Chandra to Noel Tata and it’s time to sing praises to Noel Tata! Just like the Tata board, many of these political professionals are looking to unemployment!” he said.During Bhat’s career with the Tata group, he held several senior leadership roles, including brand custodian at Tata Sons, managing director of Tata Global Beverages, and chief operating officer of Titan’s watches and accessories business.
Article Summary: Harish Bhat has resigned from Trent, the retailer chaired by Noel Tata. Bhat, 63, served on Trent’s board for 12 years. He continues to serve on the boards of Tata Starbucks and Infiniti Retail (Croma) His resignation has revived debate about shifting loyalties.

Article Title: Tata Trusts row: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust files response to commissioner
Article Text:
MCC had initially directed SDTT to file its response by Oct 12, but granted the trust additional time, extending the deadline to Oct 19.

MUMBAI: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) on Monday filed its response with Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC) to complaints lodged by trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh , meeting the extended October 19 deadline for its submission.The complaints sought an inquiry into SDTT’s administration and governance, including the appointments of Noel Tata as a perpetual trustee and his son, Neville Tata, as a trustee. They further alleged that Srinivasan was excluded from the decision-making process surrounding Neville’s appointment and questioned the involvement of SDTT and Noel in the commercial and strategic affairs of Tata Sons.A Tata Trusts spokesperson confirmed the response had been filed but declined to share the contents of the submission, which runs into dozens of pages.MCC had initially directed SDTT to file its response by October 12, but granted the trust additional time, extending the deadline to October 19.The complainants had also sought interim directions, including the suspension or removal of trustees from SDTT, restrictions on Noel’s participation in matters concerning Tata Sons, and a bar on his exercising voting rights on behalf of SDTT at Tata Sons shareholder meetings.SDTT is the largest shareholder in Tata Sons, with a 28% stake, followed by Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) with 24%.MCC had barred SRTT from holding trustee meetings until an investigation into separate complaints filed by Srinivasan is completed. The latest complaints, filed on Sept 25 by Srinivasan and Singh, followed disagreements over the future of Tata Sons, including whether the company should remain unlisted and how liquidity should be provided to minority shareholder Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group.Srinivasan had alleged that Noel had taken a direct role in identifying, negotiating and facilitating liquidity for the SP Group through the monetisation of Tata Sons shareholding.
Article Summary: Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) on Monday filed its response with Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC) to complaints lodged by trustees Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. MCC had initially directed SDTT to file its response by Oct 12, but granted the trust additional time, extending the deadline to Oct 19.

Article Title: Rising crude, lender-margin squeeze take toll on Dalal-Street
Article Text:
Disappointing quarterly earnings from major private lenders, elevated crude oil prices and continued foreign investor outflows added to the pressure

MUMBAI: Benchmark indices snapped a two-day winning streak on Monday, with sensex falling 876 points, or 1.2%, to 73,853 and Nifty declining 257 points, or 1.1%, to 22,889 as selling in private sector banks and IT stocks weighed on sentiment. Sensex opened 211 points lower at 74,518, while Nifty started 63 points down at 23,083. Selling intensified through the session. Axis Bank was the biggest laggard among Nifty constituents, falling 4.2%. HDFC Bank declined 2.3% and Tata Motors lost more than 3%. On the other hand, JSW Steel gained 2%, ONGC rose 1.4% and State Bank of India advanced 1.2%.According to Vinay Rajani, senior technical research analyst at HDFC Securities, Nifty is approaching support at 22,800, where it could resume its uptrend. “However, a decisive break below the positional support at 22,500 would weaken the bullish outlook and warrant caution,” he said. Most sectoral indices ended lower, with private banks, IT and FMCG among the worst hit. The Nifty PSU Bank index was the only sectoral index to finish in positive territory, gaining 2.5%, while the Nifty Private Bank index fell 1.9%. Union Bank gained 5.3%, highlighting the divergence between public and private sector lenders.Disappointing quarterly earnings from major private lenders, elevated crude oil prices and continued foreign investor outflows added to the pressure. Results from HDFC Bank and Axis Bank missed consensus expectations amid concerns over shrinking net interest margins. Brent crude traded around $107-108 a barrel amid geopolitical tensions and conflict risks in West Asia, raising concerns about inflation and India’s import bill. Foreign institutional investors, meanwhile, net sold equities worth Rs 1,149 crore.
Article Summary: Sensex opened 211 points lower at 74,518, while Nifty started 63 points down at 23,083. Most sectoral indices ended lower, with private banks, IT and FMCG among the worst hit. Results from HDFC Bank and Axis Bank missed consensus expectations. Foreign institutional investors, meanwhile, net sold equities worth Rs 1,149 crore.

Article Title: Indian Railways cracks down on food quality issues after passenger complaints; IRCTC partners with QCI for surprise audits on trains and stations with digital evidence to speed up action
Article Text:
Officials said the decision to introduce independent inspections followed repeated passenger complaints. (Image for representative purpose only)

Addressing passenger complaints on food

IRCTC Food checks

Providing meals that are prepared at designated base kitchens.

Setting up modern base kitchens at some select locations.

Installing CCTV cameras in base kitchens that enables real-time surveillance and improves the monitoring of food preparation.

Identifying and using popular branded raw materials for preparing food.

Appointing Food Safety Supervisors at base kitchens to oversee food safety and hygienic practices.

Deploying IRCTC supervisors on board trains.

Carrying out deep cleaning at regular intervals and conducting periodic pest-control activities in base kitchens and pantry cars.

The food quality on trains may see an improvement with the Quality Council of India (QCI) looking to appoint certified professionals to carry out independent, technology-enabled checks of food safety and hygiene at railway stations and aboard trains across the Indian Railways network.Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited ( IRCTC ) has entered into a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with QCI to strengthen compliance with food safety and hygiene standards across the railway system, according to a statement issued by the Railway Ministry"Under this strategic alliance, QCI will deploy certified professionals to conduct intense, unannounced quarterly and half-yearly inspection cycles," the ministry said.It added: "These audits will enforce strict compliance with statutory Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regulations and international culinary standards."Officials said the decision to introduce independent inspections followed repeated passenger complaints about poor food quality and unhygienic catering practices. The ministry subsequently decided to bring in a third-party agency to audit food safety and hygiene."To eliminate data tampering and guarantee absolute transparency, the audit process will leverage QCI's pioneer digital infrastructure," the ministry said.As part of the system, inspectors will use a mobile application to record their findings, with geo-tagging, time-stamps and photographic evidence made mandatory.Audit reports will have to be submitted within 24 hours, allowing operational shortcomings to be identified promptly and enabling corrective and preventive measures to be tracked against vendors found violating the prescribed standards.Explaining how the initiative would benefit passengers, the ministry said: "Rigorous independent screening across trains ensures passengers are protected from subpar onboard meal preparation."It also highlighted the need for uniform hygiene standards at station-based catering facilities, stating: "Complete standardisation guarantees immaculate cooking environments across all major station-based static units," the ministry added.The ministry said the use of digitally documented evidence and the requirement to submit reports within 24 hours would help speed up corrective action and the imposition of penalties against catering licensees where necessary.Indian Railways serves an average of around 58 crore meals annually. Over the past three years, IRCTC has taken punitive action in response to complaints against several vendors.According to a recent PIB release, these measures include imposing fines of Rs 5.13 crore, issuing 54 show-cause notices, terminating six contracts and debarring licensees for violations related to food quality and hygiene. IRCTC has made the list of debarred licensees available on its website.Railway and IRCTC officials, including Food Safety Officers, carry out routine as well as surprise inspections to check food quality, hygiene, safety and compliance with applicable regulations.These inspections examine several aspects of catering operations, including food safety, staff deployment, upkeep of equipment, cleanliness and adherence to prescribed standards. They also seek to encourage best practices in food handling, storage and preparation.According to Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s recent reply to a question in Rajya Sabha, IRCTC is taking the following measures on food quality:
Article Summary: Quality Council of India (QCI) looking to appoint certified professionals to carry out independent, technology-enabled checks of food safety and hygiene at railway stations and aboard trains. Officials said the decision to introduce independent inspections followed repeated passenger complaints. Indian Railways serves an average of around 58 crore meals annually.

Article Title: India's trade deal with New Zealand kicks in today
Article Text:
Sensitive products such as dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions

India-NZ trade deal

NEW DELHI: The India-New Zealand trade agreement is set to kick in from Tuesday, allowing duty-free entry for all products from the country, apart from opening the doors for professionals and investment of $20 billion.On Monday, the first-ever export of a JCB machine from India to New Zealand was flagged off by commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal , with farm products, gems and jewellery, engineering, sports goods, footwear and leather also set to sail on Tuesday, when the agreement comes into force."Ours is a winning partnership, both on and off the field. The success of this agreement will be measured by the opportunities it creates and the difference it makes to the lives of the people of New Zealand and India. For India, 100% duty-free access to the New Zealand market opens significant new opportunities for our exporters, particularly MSMEs, artisans, farmers, and women entrepreneurs. For our farmers, the agreement combines new opportunities with appropriate safeguards," Goyal said."Agricultural Productivity Partnership is a key component of the Agreement, extending cooperation beyond tariff concessions to bring global technology, training and best practices to Indian farmers. It includes dedicated Action Plans for kiwifruit, apples and honey, with cooperation also extending to horticulture, forestry, livestock and fisheries," an official statement said.To protect farmers, dairy producers, fisherfolk and rural communities, sensitive products such as dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions, govt said.
Article Summary: The India-New Zealand trade agreement is set to kick in from Tuesday. It will allow duty-free entry for all products from the country, apart from opening the doors for professionals and investment of $20 billion. Sensitive products such as dairy, sugar, edible oils and key agricultural commodities remain excluded from concessions.

Article Title: Trade margins on 137 cancer drugs capped, but will bills get lower?
Article Text:
‘Hospitals may still find ways to hike charges of other items and packages,’ warns a civil society group

What are the other charges

Wider rationalisation of margins across products needed: Experts

NEW DELHI: Govt’s move to cap trade margins at 30% of MRP on 137 cancer drugs, covering over 1,000 medicine brands, puts the focus on actual patient savings, with effective implementation and monitoring needed to ensure it translates into lower medical bills.The cap could narrow the gap between prices at which medicines are supplied to hospitals and their MRPs, but it may have a limited impact on overall cost of healthcare as hospitals may seek to offset lower margins by raising charges on consumables, diagnostics or procedures, public health and industry experts told TOI. A similar trend was seen after cardiac stent prices were capped in 2017, when several private hospital chains raised angioplasty package rates, they said.Cancer drugs including branded and generic, both by domestic firms and MNCs, should be made available at revised prices from Nov 9. Much of the supply of these life-saving injectables goes straight to hospitals, so the order makes them responsible for charging revised prices.Experts said wider rationalisation of margins across medical products, alongside closer scrutiny of hospital charges, may be needed to substantially reduce medical bills.Hospital stocks were down on BSE on Monday, following the govt notification on Oct 17.The MRP of certain cancer drugs are up to Rs 5 lakh per vial or pack, including a combination of pertuzumab and trastuzumab, atezolizumab, teclistamab, inotuzumab ozogamicin and daratumumab.“The success of this measure will, however, depend equally on timely implementation across manufacturers, distributors and hospitals. A trade margin of 30% should not be misconstrued as a 30% profit margin for hospitals. The defined trade margin applies across the distribution chain, and the basis of calculation and applicability of the prescribed margin at different stages of the supply chain, should be clearly communicated to avoid any misunderstanding,” Girdhar Gyani, director general at the Association of Healthcare Providers, which represents over 20,000 hospitals and healthcare providers, told TOI.Oncology is a significant revenue stream for hospitals, with expensive cancer drugs and cost of care contributing to high treatment costs. The margin cap could put pressure on hospital earnings, raising concerns over whether lower margins could affect the viability of such services. “Affordability must be viewed across the entire cancer-care pathway, from screening and diagnosis to treatment,” said Mayur Sirdesai, co-founding partner at Somerset Indus Capital.“The impact of TMR on affordability and patient access will need to be evaluated, said Sudarshan Jain, secretary-general of Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance.Public health experts said the margin rationalisation may not be enough to reduce costs for patients. “Prices of these medicines will still remain out of the reach for many patients. Also, hospitals may find ways to hike charges of other items and packages,” said KM Gopakumar of Third World Network, a civil society group.
Article Summary: Govt's move to cap trade margins at 30% of MRP on 137 cancer drugs, covering over 1,000 medicine brands, puts the focus on actual patient savings. ‘Hospitals may still find ways to hike charges of other items and packages,’ warns a civil society group.
